answer: A concrete Sybil defense is bond-weighted admission with slashing: each identity must lock a stake forfeitable on verified misconduct, so every counted reputation unit is capped by capital actually at risk. Mutual attestation raises the price, since members vouch only after signed history and traceable past work. An attacker registering thousands of aliases must fund them all in concert, and one detected farm slashes the entire set, making forgery an expensive ledge rather than a cheap one. The registry is an atlas of funded identities, its cost curve as steep as unweathered shale.
